  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror

  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

def content_dir(site):
    return os.path.join(site, "src", "content", "docs")


def pages(site):
    """{slug: path} for every page, the home page's slug being ''."""
    found = {}
    base = content_dir(site)
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(base, "**", "*.md*"), recursive=True):
        slug = os.path.relpath(path, base).rsplit(".", 1)[0]
        found["" if slug == "index" else slug] = path
    return found

### Patches

The property tools (`set_video`, `set_audio`, `set_text`, `set_shape`,
`set_graphic`, `set_clip`, `set_action_end`) take a `patch` object, and it
merges into what the clip already has:

- Keys you leave out keep their values, at every depth. A patch of just
  `{shadow: {blur: 20}}` keeps the shadow's colour, angle and distance.
- A key set to `null` clears it.
- A list replaces the whole list (`filters`, for example: send the whole
  stack, or `[]` to clear it).
- An unknown key or a wrong value is refused, naming its dotted path and the
  value you sent, such as `filters[1].kind`. Nothing is dropped, corrected or
  clamped on the way.

### What a call answers

Every answer comes back in band, as the tool's result, so a model can read it
and correct itself. A refused or invalid call is an ordinary tool result
with `isError: true` whose text is the sentence, never a transport or
JSON-RPC error. A call that changed nothing is marked the same way; its
sentence, below, says that nothing was wrong. Only an MCP method the server
does not know gets a JSON-RPC "method not found".

**An edit that landed** answers `ok: true`, the ids it created (`new_clips`,
`new_tracks`, `new_markers`, `new_media`, only those that apply), anything
the tool adds of its own, and a short `project` summary: name, path, width,
height, fps, duration, playhead, counts of tracks, clips, markers and media,
the selection, `unsaved_changes`, and `missing_media` when a file is gone.
Every edit is exactly one undo step, however many clips it touched.

**An edit that did not happen** is one of two kinds, and the answer says
which. Neither leaves an undo step, so it is safe to retry.

| Answer | Meaning |
|---|---|
| "*Step* made no change: the project is already in that state." | Nothing was wrong. The project already says what you asked. |
| "*Step* was refused at *op*: *reason*" | A rule declined the edit. The reason names the op and what you can act on — which track is locked, which clips still use a media file, how far two clips would overlap, or the argument that lets the call through (`with_clips: true`, `ripple: true`). |

**An argument the tool does not take** is refused before anything runs:
"*tool* does not take *x*. It takes *a*, *b* and *c*." A value a tool cannot
read is refused by name rather than ignored.

## Editing inside a nest
### Clip properties

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `set_video` | *op* — position, scale, rotation, opacity, crop, corners, shadow, colour and grading, chroma key, filters, reflection, spotlight, motion and Remove Background (`cutout`: the clip drawn as its subject, where its masks are cached; a picture's are made from the picture itself as soon as the cutout is set — person segmentation, or for `subject: "foreground"`, an image clip's only, the foreground instance mask — and `analyze_cutout` answers where they stand), and Text Behind Subject (`behind_subject`: the clip cut by the person of every cut-out clip behind it), and Hide While Silent (`hide_silent {media, pre_roll, hold, fade}`: the clip fades out while that media's speech is silent; the media's speech is saved first in the same step when it has none), and Motion Blur (`motion_blur`, 0–1 of a frame: the clip, and its moving cursor, blurred along their motion in the preview, `render_frame` and every export; refused above 0 on a nest or adjustment clip). |
| `set_audio` | *op* — volume, mute, fades, ducking, mono, keep pitch, pan, compression and noise reduction. |
| `set_text` | *op* — a text clip's words and typography. |
| `set_shape` | *op* — a shape clip's geometry and paint. |
| `set_graphic` | *op* — which module a graphic clip draws, its size, length and props. |
| `set_clip` | *op* — a clip's name and colour label (**Clip ▸ Rename…**, ⇧⌘R; **Clip ▸ Label**). |

See [Canvas and layers](canvas-and-layers.md), [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md), [Audio](audio.md), [Colour grading](color-grading.md) and [Graphics](graphics.md).

### Animation

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `add_action` | *op* — an animation span on a clip, in clip time; its end state starts empty. |
| `add_zoom_action` | *op* — an animated zoom to a `region` (`fit` or `fill`), or back out with `region: null`. |
| `switch_layout` | *op* — a camera layout at `at`: the `camera` clip and the screen behind it in `corner` (`shape`, `corner`), `side_by_side`, `stacked`, `camera_full` or `screen_only`, eased over 0.5 s and held on later clips until the next switch or `through`; a zoom in the way is refused unless `nest: true`; an omitted `focus` is filled from the camera clip's cached person masks, and the answer's `focus` is what was sent (Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸, the Picture sub-tab's Layout section). |
| `reframe_clip` | *op* — frames one clip on the current canvas: `follow` `subject`, `face`, `person` or `salient` follows what is found in the clip on this Mac (the tool analyses its window and waits up to 60 s; past that it answers `analyzing` and changes nothing — call it again), `center` holds the window on the picture's centre at `zoom` (1–4 × fill), `fit` shows the whole picture, `keep` rescales from `from_width × from_height`; `cursor` follows a screen recording's recorded pointer from its media's cursor file (read at once, no analysis, no wait), arriving on each click and holding still while typing, and a clip whose media has a cursor file is refused by the face-following kinds; `layout` re-lays a camera clip's camera layouts and its screen's on the current canvas from `from_width × from_height`, refused naming a switch edited by hand; `speaker` frames a wide shot on whoever is talking, from the microphone clips in `mics` (read as Switch by Speaker reads them; each matched to the face whose mouth moves with it, or named with `mic_faces`, faces numbered left to right), a cut at each change held at least 2 s, two at once framed together when they fit, refused naming each face's place when the match is weak; written as the clip's position and scale and one action per move, with a blurred copy on `backdrop` behind any span that shows the whole picture. A clip with actions is refused, unless `keep` and none moves or scales it ([Vertical and framing](vertical-and-framing.md)). |
| `set_action` | *op* — moves, re-times or re-curves an action. |
| `set_action_end` | *op* — what an action animates to: video, audio, text, a graphic's props, or a `speed`. |
| `remove_action` | *op* — removes an action. |

See [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md) and [Speed](speed.md).

### Transitions

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `add_transition` | *op* — makes an overlap at a hard cut and puts a transition on it (**Clip ▸ Transition**); `ripple: true` makes it by moving clips instead. |
| `set_transition` | *op* — the transition into a clip; `kind: null` removes it. |
| `set_transition_duration` | *op* — makes a transition last `duration` by moving the clip. |
| `set_transition_style` | *op* — the easing curve and whether the sound crossfades. |

See [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).

### Tracks, markers and canvas

extension AgentServer {
    /// The transition rows, given the two SENTENCES the clip group already
    /// hoisted — the ticks note and the clip-id prose — so neither is spelled
    /// a second time.
    func transitionTools(ticks: String, clipDescription: String) -> [[String: Any]] {
        return [
            opTool(
                "add_transition",
                "Makes an overlap at the HARD CUT before a clip and puts a transition on it — "
                    + "Clip ▸ Transition ▸ <kind> on a clip that abuts the one before it. The "
                    + "overlap is built out of material the two clips already have (the source "
                    + "before the incoming clip's in point, and after the outgoing clip's "
                    + "out point), so NOTHING else on the timeline moves and the pair's outer "
                    + "edges stay exactly where they were. duration is snapped down to whole "
                    + "frames and CLAMPED — to each side's available material, to the "
                    + "neighbours on the track, and to the overlap rule — so a request too "
                    + "long for the media lands shorter rather than failing; a request that "
                    + "clamps below one frame is refused. An affected track already outside "
                    + "the overlap rule is refused by that rule before fitting. align center takes half from "
                    + "each side (an odd frame goes to the incoming clip, and a side with "
                    + "nothing to give passes its share to the other), before takes it all "
                    + "from the incoming clip's head, after all from the outgoing clip's tail. "
                    + "kind absent uses the clip's stored kind if it has one and "
                    + "cross_dissolve otherwise; a stored transition keeps its curve and "
                    + "crossfade, a new one is eased at both ends and crossfades its sound. "
                    + "The incoming clip's actions move with its new first frame, so a zoom "
                    + "stays on the source frame it was drawn over. Errors when duration is "
                    + "not positive and when the clip is NOT at a hard cut, naming which of: "
                    + "no clip before it, a gap, an overlap that already exists (use "
                    + "set_transition or set_transition_duration for that one). With "
                    + "ripple true the overlap is made by MOVING instead — the sheet's Shift "
                    + "Clips Left button when neither clip has footage beyond the cut: no "
                    + "material is read and align is ignored, and the incoming clip plus "
                    + "every clip at or after the cut on every unlocked track slides left by "
                    + "duration, so the timeline gets that much shorter and no clip's source "
                    + "window changes. It is capped at half the shorter of the two clips and "
                    + "limited to the greatest whole-frame shift that leaves every moved "
                    + "track inside the overlap rule, including after clips cross; a clip "
                    + "on another track pushed into its neighbour gets a cross_dissolve; "
                    + "markers do not move.",
    /// `set_text`'s clause for format version 9's three word-caption keys,
    /// spliced into its patch description by `AgentCatalog+Properties.swift`
    /// (`AgentCatalog+Clips.swift`, over the cap, gave it up as a pure move in
    /// issue batch B86, and the patch descriptions followed in grading GR1).
    /// The three looks of format version 12 (spec §11 W-12, W-13) are
    /// taught here: `glide`, `active_fill` and `pause_dim`.
    static let textWordsClause: String =
        ", case (as_written|upper — applied before layout; it never changes the word count), "
        + "words (one {start, end} per whitespace token of content, in clip ticks, or [] for "
        + "an untimed page — a content change that alters the count must send words: [] in "
        + "the same patch), word_style (null or {mode: highlight|build, active_color, "
        + "active_scale 1–1.5, active_pill {color, padding, radius, glide}, spoken_color, "
        + "upcoming_color, active_fill, pause_dim 0–1} — how the word being said is drawn; it "
        + "replaces animation. Three looks, each off by default: active_pill.glide (true|false) "
        + "slides the pill from the word before to the active one over 0.2 s, or sooner when "
        + "the next word starts sooner, instead of jumping; active_fill (true|false) fills the "
        + "active word left to right from its start to its end, taking 0.6 s at most — the "
        + "part said in active_color and the rest in upcoming_color, or not yet drawn in build "
        + "mode; in highlight mode it shows only where those two colours differ; pause_dim "
        + "fades the words and the pill to 1 − pause_dim of their opacity in a pause of 0.25 s "
        + "or more — after one word's end until the next one's start, before a late first "
        + "word, and after the last word until the clip ends — over 0.1 s each way, and outside "
        + "0–1 it is refused)"

    /// One of `transcribe`'s three look booleans (spec §11 W-15): what it
    /// does, then the rule all three share, with the styles it applies with
    /// read off `CaptionLooks.Look.styleList` — the list its refusal prints —
    /// never typed.
    static func captionLookProperty(
        _ look: CaptionLooks.Look, _ does: String
    ) -> [String: Any] {
        [
            "type": "boolean",
            "description": does + " Default false, and never what the sheet last chose. It "
                + "applies with style " + look.styleList + ": true is refused by name with any "
                + "other style or with place false, where it would show nothing; false is "
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    "video": "Show this clip's picture.",
                    "audio": "Play this clip's sound.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "set_transition",
                "Sets the transition INTO a clip — the one that plays across its overlap with "
                    + "the clip before it on the same track. The transition's duration IS that "
                    + "overlap, so a clip with no overlap ignores it: make one with move_clip or "
                    + "set_transition_duration. kind null removes it.",
                [
                    "clip": clipDescription,
                    // The null beside the core's thirteen names, and the
                    // required-ness that keeps a forgotten kind from becoming
                    // one, are both declared rows
                    // (`AgentCatalog+Declarations.swift`).
                    "kind": "The transition, or null to remove it.",
                ]),
            opTool(
                "set_transition_duration",
                "Makes a clip's transition last `duration` by MOVING the clip so its overlap "
                    + "with the clip before it equals that. Refused on a track's first clip and past "
                    + "half the shorter clip (snapped down), naming that limit.",
                ["clip": clipDescription, "duration": "Overlap length, \(ticks)"]),
        ]
        rows += actionTools(ticks: ticks, clipDescription: clipDescription)
        return rows
    }

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`

  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting

  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

Both bounds are cut by `split_under_playhead`; each piece wholly inside starts at `f(s)` and lasts `f(e) − f(s)`: a constant media piece plays at speed × `rate`, held to its media, a ramped one scales its whole profile by `rate` (SR-19), and a text, shape, still, image, graphic (its `length` kept) or adjustment piece scales its start and duration; actions keep their fraction; `keep_pitch`, when given, is set on each media piece's audio. Everything at or after `to` moves by `to′ − to` with its linked partners (AU-91); markers inside map through `f` and markers after move with the shift (none inside a nest). input.content:
---
title: "Tools: picture and grade (set_video)"
description: Change a clip's position, crop, effects, cut-out, cursor, motion and grade from an agent with one patch tool, set_video.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

`set_video` is the one tool behind everything a clip's picture does: where it sits, how it's cropped, its effects, its motion and its grade. It takes a list of clips and a patch, and this page lists every key the patch can hold.

<AtAGlance
  tools="set_video"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Picture sub-tab', 'Clip tab ▸ Color sub-tab', 'Dragging on the canvas']}
/>

## `set_video`

Merges a patch into each clip's own video properties, as one undo step however many clips it names. It mirrors the Clip tab's [Picture sub-tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) and [Color sub-tab](/color/color-tab/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
| `patch` | object | Yes | The properties to change. The rest of this page lists its keys. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

```json
{ "clips": [12, 14], "patch": { "opacity": 0.8, "shadow": { "blur": 20 } } }
```

**How a patch merges.** A key you leave out keeps its value, inside a nested object too, so `{shadow: {blur: 20}}` keeps the shadow's colour, angle and distance. On a clip that has no shadow yet, the keys you left out take the defaults listed below. `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `motion`, `look`, `cursor`, `cutout` and `hide_silent` set to `null` clear that property. `filters` and `obscure` are lists, so each replaces whole: send the full list, or `[]` to clear it. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).

**Colours.** A colour is four numbers, `[r, g, b, a]`, each 0 to 1. Three numbers are refused, and so is a value outside the range. The chroma key's colour is the one exception: three numbers, with no alpha.

**What it answers.** The usual edit answer: `ok` and the `project` summary. If the patch changes nothing, the call says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

**When it refuses.**

- A key or value the patch doesn't know is an error naming its dotted path, array indices included, and the value you sent, such as `filters[1].kind`. Nothing is dropped, corrected or clamped.
- A number outside its range is an error naming the key, the range and the number.
- A clip with no video properties is an error: "clip 7 has no video properties".
- The sections below list what a particular kind of clip can't take.

### Which key does what

| Keys | Section |
| --- | --- |
| `x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `blend` | [Transform](#transform-position-scale-rotation-opacity-and-blend) |
| `crop`, `corner_radius` | [Crop and corners](#crop-and-corners) |
| `shadow`, `chroma`, `filters`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `obscure` | [Effects](#effects-shadow-chroma-key-filters-reflection-spotlight-and-obscure) |
| `cutout` | [Remove Background](#cutout) |
| `behind_subject` | [Text Behind Subject](#behind_subject) |
| `cursor` | [The recorded cursor](#cursor) |
| `motion` | [Motion presets](#motion) |
| `motion_blur` | [Motion blur](#motion_blur) |
| `hide_silent` | [Hide While Silent](#hide_silent) |
| `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, `qualifier` | [Light and colour](#color), [wheels](#wheels), [curves](#curves), [looks and LUTs](#look), [the qualifier](#qualifier) |

### On an adjustment clip

An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no picture of its own. Only `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, the sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters, and `opacity` (the grade's strength) do anything there, and `qualifier` narrows which pixels they reach. The blur, sharpen and pixelate filters and any blend mode are errors, such as "clip 7 is an adjustment clip and cannot take the blur filter".

### Animate a property

`set_video` changes the clip's base value, which holds for the clip's whole length. To change a value over time, use `add_action` then `set_action_end`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/). `motion` and `hide_silent` can't be animated.

## Transform: position, scale, rotation, opacity and blend

The clip's picture is centred on the canvas centre plus `x` and `y`, scaled, then rotated about that same centre. The [Transform section](/canvas/transform/) and dragging on the canvas change the same values.

| Key | What it does | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x`, `y` | The clip's centre, in canvas pixels from the canvas centre. `y` runs down. | Any number |
| `scale` | The size. 1 is native pixels. | 0.01 to 10 |
| `rotation` | Degrees about the clip's centre. Positive turns clockwise on screen. | Any number |
| `opacity` | How solid the clip is. | 0 to 1 |
| `blend` | How the clip combines with what's already on the canvas. | `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `add`, `overlay`, `darken`, `lighten`, `difference` |

`normal` is the default. A blend mode needs something under it. Over the empty canvas, `multiply`, `darken` and `overlay` read black, while `screen`, `add`, `lighten` and `difference` change nothing, so `add_background` is usually the call to make first.

A blend is forced to `normal` for the length of a cross dissolve, so the frame there can differ from the value `get_project` reports. A nest clip can't take a blend mode other than `normal`. See [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/).

## Crop and corners

| Key | What it does | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crop` | `{l, t, r, b}`, the pixels to remove from each edge of the source. Cropping never shifts what's left. | Each 0 or more |
| `corner_radius` | Rounds the corners of the cropped picture, in source pixels, before it's rotated. | 0 or more |

The opposite edges have to leave something behind: `l` plus `r` must be less than the source's width, and `t` plus `b` less than its height. See [Crop](/canvas/crop/) and [Corner radius](/canvas/corner-radius/).

## Effects: shadow, chroma key, filters, reflection, spotlight and obscure

Each of these is off until you set it. `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection` and `spotlight` are objects that merge, and `null` clears one. `filters` and `obscure` are lists that replace whole.

### Shadow

`shadow` is `null` or an object. See [Shadow](/effects/shadow/).

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | The shadow's colour. | Four numbers | Black |
| `opacity` | How strong it is. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |
| `blur` | How soft it is, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 12 |
| `angle` | The direction, in degrees. 0 is to the right, turning counter-clockwise. | Any number | 315 |
| `distance` | How far it falls, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 8 |

### Chroma key

`chroma` is `null` or an object. See [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/).

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | The colour to remove, as three numbers with no alpha. | Each 0 to 1 | Green, `[0, 1, 0]` |
| `tolerance` | How far from the key a colour can be and still go. | 0 to 1 | 0.2 |
| `softness` | How gradually the edge falls off. | 0 to 1 | 0.1 |
| `spill` | How much of the key's colour to take off what's left. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |

### Filters

`filters` is a list of up to four `{kind, amount}` objects, applied in order, so blur then sepia differs from sepia then blur. `kind` is `blur`, `sharpen`, `pixelate`, `sepia`, `noir`, `vignette` or `invert`. `amount` is 0 to 1, where 0 does nothing. A left-out `kind` is `blur` and a left-out `amount` is 0.5. A fifth filter is an error, never dropped. See [Filters](/effects/filters/).

```json
{ "filters": [{ "kind": "noir", "amount": 1 }, { "kind": "vignette", "amount": 0.4 }] }
```

### Reflection

`reflection` is `null` or an object. See [Reflection](/effects/reflection/).

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opacity` | How strong the reflection is where it touches the clip. | 0 to 1 | 0.35 |
| `height` | How much of the clip is mirrored, as a fraction of its cropped height. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |
| `gap` | The space between the clip and the reflection, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 0 |
| `falloff` | How fast it fades, as a fraction of the cropped height. 0 doesn't fade, and 1 reaches transparent exactly at `height`. | 0 to 1 | 1 |

### Spotlight

`spotlight` is `null` or an object. It dims everything outside a shape and can magnify what's inside it. See [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/).

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | The shape. | `rect`, `ellipse` | `rect` |
| `x`, `y` | The shape's centre, in source pixels from the centre of the cropped picture, `y` down. It can sit outside the picture. | Any number | 0 |
| `width`, `height` | The shape's size, in source pixels. | Above 0 | 480, 270 |
| `feather` | How many source pixels the edge blurs over. | 0 or more | 40 |
| `dim` | How much darker it is outside. 0 changes nothing, and 1 is black. | 0 to 1 | 0.6 |
| `zoom` | How much to magnify what's inside. 1 is no zoom. | 1 to 2 | 1 |

Because the box is in source pixels, it stays on the picture when the clip is moved, scaled or rotated.

### Obscure

`obscure` is a list of up to four regions, each hiding what's under it. It uses the spotlight's frame for its centre and box. See [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | The shape. | `rect`, `ellipse` | `rect` |
| `x`, `y` | The region's centre, in source pixels from the centre of the cropped picture. | Any number | 0 |
| `width`, `height` | The region's size, in source pixels. | Above 0 | 480, 270 |
| `feather` | How many source pixels the effect ramps in over. | 0 or more | 20 |
| `kind` | How it hides. | `blur`, `pixelate` | `pixelate` |
| `amount` | How strongly it hides. | 0 to 1 | 1 |

## `cutout`

Remove Background: draws the clip as its subject alone, from masks made on your Mac. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Remove Background** and the Picture sub-tab's **Background** section. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).

`cutout` is `null` or an object. `{cutout: {}}` turns it on with all five defaults, an object merges, and `null` removes it.

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | What to keep. `foreground` is the picture's foreground object, and only an image clip can take it. | `person`, `foreground` | `person` |
| `quality` | The mask quality. `best` is refused, because Best masks aren't made yet. | `standard` | `standard` |
| `background` | `remove` draws only the subject. `keep` draws the clip whole, which [Text Behind Subject](#behind_subject) uses. | `remove`, `keep` | `remove` |
| `edge` | Shrinks or grows the outline. | −1 to 1 | 0 |
| `feather` | Softens the outline. | 0 to 1 | 0 |

A media, still or image clip can take a cutout. A text, shape, graphic, adjustment or nest clip is refused, and so is `foreground` on a media or still clip.

**When the masks are made.** They're made as soon as the cutout is set, and `analyze_cutout` says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/). The cut-out draws in the preview, `render_frame` and every export:

- The preview draws a frame whole while its mask isn't made yet.
- `render_frame` waits up to 30 s for its masks, then draws the clip uncut and says so.
- An export waits for every mask it draws.
- A stretch of the clip where no person was found draws uncut.

**In an action.** `edge` and `feather` animate, and `background` switches when the action ends. `subject` and `quality` are refused there, and an action can't switch the cutout off. On a clip with no cutout, an action's cutout keys do nothing.

## `behind_subject`

Text Behind Subject: `true` cuts the clip at each moment by the person of every cut-out clip on a track behind it in the same container, so the person stands in front of it. A cut-out clip in front of it doesn't cut it. Any clip with a cutout counts, with `background` set to `remove` or `keep`. The default is `false`. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Behind Subject** section. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).

Any clip that draws a picture can take it, except an adjustment clip or a nest clip, which are refused. In an action it switches when the action ends. [`text_behind_subject`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) places a title this way in one step.

## `cursor`

Styles the cursor recorded in the media's cursor file, as it's drawn on this clip. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Cursor** section. See [Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/).

`cursor` is `null` or an object. `{cursor: {}}` stores all eight defaults, and an object merges. A value out of range is refused, never clamped.

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show` | Whether the cursor is drawn. | `true`, `false` | `true` |
| `scale` | Its size. | 0.25 to 8 | 1 |
| `style` | `recorded` draws the recorded image, and `arrow` draws Frame Job's own arrow. `recorded` also draws the arrow at a moment the file holds no cursor image. | `recorded`, `arrow` | `recorded` |
| `smoothing` | How much the path is smoothed. | 0 to 1 | 0 |
| `hide_idle` | Seconds of no activity before it hides. `null` never hides it. | `null`, 0.5 to 30 | `null` |
| `clicks` | What a click draws. | `none`, `ripple` | `none` |
| `click_color` | The ripple's colour, as a CSS colour. | Any CSS colour | `#ffffffcc` |
| `click_size` | The ripple's size. | 0.25 to 4 | 1 |

**In an action.** `scale` and `click_size` animate. `show`, `style`, `clicks` and `click_color` switch when the action ends. `smoothing` and `hide_idle` have no effect in an action, so write them here. On a clip with no cursor, every cursor key in an action switches at the end, so give the clip one first with `{cursor: {}}` if you want them to animate.

## `motion`

What the clip does on its way in, on its way out and all the way through. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Motion ▸**. See [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).

`motion` is `null` or `{in, out, during}`. The three slots merge: a slot you leave out keeps what's stored, a slot set to `null` clears that slot, and `{motion: null}` clears all three.

| Slot | Keys | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in`, `out` | `kind`, `duration` | `kind` is `fade`, `zoom_in`, `zoom_out`, `slide_left`, `slide_right`, `slide_up`, `slide_down`, `spin` or `pop`. `duration` is in ticks, measured from the clip's first or last frame. |
| `during` | `kind`, `amount`, `period` | `kind` is `pulse`, `shake`, `spin`, `bounce` or `drift`. `amount` is 0 to 1. `period` is in ticks, and `drift` ignores it. |

```json
{ "motion": { "in": { "kind": "fade", "duration": 300000 }, "during": null } }
```

A slot you name without its keys starts from a half-second `fade`, or for `during` a `pulse` of amount 0.5 and period 1 s.

The durations snap to the frame grid, and the period snaps with a floor of one frame, so `get_project` can answer with a number near the one you sent. `in` plus `out` longer than the clip scales both down to meet, rather than being refused. A negative duration, or a period under one tick, is an error.

`motion` can't be animated: `set_action_end` refuses it. `get_project` reports the clip as if it weren't moving, because the preset only becomes placement when a frame is drawn.

## `motion_blur`

Blurs the clip, and its moving cursor, along their motion. It mirrors the **Motion Blur** row in the Picture sub-tab's **Transform** section. See [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/).

`motion_blur` is 0 to 1, the shutter as a fraction of one canvas frame. 0 is off and the default, and 0.5 is a 180° shutter. It animates in an action, and draws in the preview, `render_frame` and every export.

Anything above 0 is refused on a nest clip, so set it on the clips inside, and on an adjustment clip. The clip draws sharp under a transition, a routed dissolve, a matte, Behind Subject or a drop shadow.

## `hide_silent`

Fades the clip out while a media's speech is silent, and back in just before it speaks. It's usually a camera over a screen recording. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Hide While Silent** section. See [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/).

`hide_silent` is `null` or an object.

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | Required. The id of the media, with sound, whose speech the clip follows. | A media id | |
| `pre_roll` | How long before speech the clip is fully in, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 120,000 (0.2 s) |
| `hold` | How long after speech it stays, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 900,000 (1.5 s) |
| `fade` | How long the fade takes, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 180,000 (0.3 s) |

```json
{ "hide_silent": { "media": 3, "hold": 600000 } }
```

The fade follows the clips of that media in the nearest container where one plays: the clip's own, then each nest around it. Where none plays, the clip stays visible. These three times don't snap to the frame grid.

If the media has no saved speech, this call saves it from the on-device voice detection first, in the same undo step. It's refused when the media has no sound, when its speech hasn't been detected yet ("Try again in a moment."), and on a nest clip, so set it on the clips inside.

Only the drawn frame sees the fade: `get_project` reads the clip's opacity without it. `hide_silent` can't be animated.

## `color`

The thirteen values of the Color sub-tab's **Light** and **Color** sections, in one object. Each is 0 for unchanged, and any subset merges. See [Light](/color/light/) and [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/).

| Key | What it does | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exposure` | Exposure, in stops. | −3 to 3 |
| `temperature` | Positive is warmer. | −1 to 1 |
| `tint` | Positive is more magenta. | −1 to 1 |
| `highlights` | The upper half of the brightness range. | −1 to 1 |
| `shadows` | The lower half of the brightness range. | −1 to 1 |
| `whites` | Stretches the picture, held at black. | −1 to 1 |
| `blacks` | Stretches the picture, held at white. | −1 to 1 |
| `vibrance` | Saturation on the colours that have little. | −1 to 1 |
| `fade` | Lifts black towards 10 % and lowers white towards 95 %. | 0 to 1 |
| `brightness` | Brightness. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
| `contrast` | Contrast. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
| `saturation` | Saturation. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
| `hue` | Turns every colour's hue this many degrees, red towards yellow towards green, keeping its Rec. 709 brightness. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −180 to 180. |

A value outside a stated range is refused.

The grade runs in this order: `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, then `filters`.

## `wheels`

Lift, gamma and gain: three colour pushes, each with its own brightness. An agent can set a push as exact numbers, which the [Wheels section](/color/wheels/) has no field for.

`wheels` is `{lift, gamma, gain}`, each `{x, y, master}`, each −1 to 1, with 0 unchanged. Any subset merges, so `{wheels: {lift: {x: 0.2, y: -0.1}}}` keeps lift's `master` and the other two wheels.

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `x`, `y` | The colour push. Its angle is the hue (0° red, 120° green, 240° blue), and its length is the strength. It must lie inside the unit circle, so `x²` plus `y²` is at most 1. |
| `master` | The brightness. |

`lift` moves black and holds white, `gain` moves white and holds black, and `gamma` moves the middle and holds both ends. A value outside these limits is refused, never clamped.

## `curves`

Writes the curves of the Color sub-tab's **Curves** section, one list of points per channel. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/) and [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/).

`curves` is an object with up to six channels. A list replaces that channel whole, and `null` removes it. Each list is 2 to 16 `[x, y]` points with `x` strictly rising.

| Channel | `x` | `y` | No change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `master`, `red`, `green`, `blue` | 0 to 1 | 0 to 1 | `y` equals `x` from 0 to 1 |
| `hue_hue` | Hue in degrees, 0 up to but not including 360 | A shift in degrees, −180 to 180 | Every `y` is 0 |
| `hue_sat` | Hue in degrees, 0 up to but not including 360 | A saturation gain, 0 to 2 | Every `y` is 1 |

```json
{ "curves": { "master": [[0, 0.05], [0.5, 0.55], [1, 1]], "hue_sat": null } }
```

A curve that changes nothing is stored as no curve. A point outside these limits is refused, never clamped.

The tone channels are smooth monotone curves through their points, flat outside the first and last `x`, and a colour goes through the colour channel after `master`. The two hue curves are smooth curves that wrap at 0 and 360. They run after the tone channels, on the colour's hue read once: a positive shift turns red towards yellow towards green, keeping brightness, and the gain scales saturation. Greys are left alone, and the effect fades in up to a chroma of 0.06.

In an action, a curve that changes nothing animates to neutral, and two curves with different point counts blend their values across the action.

## `look`

Applies one of the eight built-in looks, or an imported `.cube` LUT, at an amount. It mirrors the Color sub-tab's **Look** section and **Clip ▸ Look ▸**. See [Looks](/color/looks/) and [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).

`look` is `null` or an object. `{look: null}` removes it.

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | Which look. | `warm`, `cool`, `teal_orange`, `vivid`, `faded`, `vintage`, `dramatic`, `black_white`, `lut` | |
| `media` | The media id of the `.cube` file. Required with `lut`, and refused with any other kind. | A LUT's media id | |
| `amount` | How much of it. | 0 to 1 | 1 |

```json
{ "look": { "kind": "teal_orange", "amount": 0.6 } }
```

For a LUT, bring the file in with `import_media`, then send `{look: {kind: "lut", media: 9}}` with the id it answers.

A new kind keeps the clip's amount, and a built-in kind replaces a LUT. An amount alone needs a clip that already has a look. In an action the amount animates, and a change of kind or of LUT switches when the action ends.

## `qualifier`

Narrows which pixels an adjustment clip's grade reaches, by hue, saturation and luma. It mirrors the Color sub-tab's **Qualifier** section. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).

The qualifier is for adjustment clips only. On any other clip it's an error naming the clip. It reads the picture behind the clip, before the grade.

`qualifier` is `{hue, saturation, luma, invert, blur}`.

| Key | Keys inside it | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hue` | `center`, `width`, `softness` | In degrees. `center` is 0 to 360 and wraps. `width` is 0 to 360, fully selected about the centre. `softness` is 0 to 180, the fall-off outside each edge. A colour with a chroma under about 0.06 has no hue and is never selected by it. |
| `saturation` | `low`, `high`, `softness` | Each 0 to 1, with `low` no more than `high`. Near-black reads as 0. |
| `luma` | `low`, `high`, `softness` | Each 0 to 1, with `low` no more than `high`. Rec. 709 luma. |
| `invert` | | `true` selects everything else. |
| `blur` | | 0 to 1, 0 being off. Softens the selection by a Gaussian of 24 × `blur` canvas pixels, never the matte. It draws nothing with no range on. |

A range merges: `{hue: {}}` turns hue on at centre 30, width 50, softness 25, and saturation and luma turn on at low 0, high 1, softness 0.1. A partial range keeps the rest, and `null` turns a range off. The selection is the product of the ranges that are on. A value outside its bounds is refused, never clamped.

In an action the numbers animate, the hue centre taking the short way round, so 350 to 10 passes 0. A range turned on or off, and `invert`, switch when the action ends.

`render_frame` with `selection` set to the adjustment clip's id draws what the qualifier selects, as [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) does. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

`set_video` is the one tool behind everything a clip's picture does: where it sits, how it's cropped, its effects, its motion and its grade. It takes a list of clips and a patch, and this page lists every key the patch can hold.

<AtAGlance
  tools="set_video"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Picture sub-tab', 'Clip tab ▸ Color sub-tab', 'Dragging on the canvas']}
/>

## `set_video`

Merges a patch into each clip's own video properties, as one undo step however many clips it names. It mirrors the Clip tab's [Picture sub-tab](/canvas/picture-tab/) and [Color sub-tab](/color/color-tab/).

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clips to change, at least one. `get_project` lists their ids. |
| `patch` | object | Yes | The properties to change. The rest of this page lists its keys. |
| `scope` | integer | No | A nest id, to edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
| `project` | string | No | The path of the open project to act on, as `get_project` reports it. Leave it out for the frontmost one. |

```json
{ "clips": [12, 14], "patch": { "opacity": 0.8, "shadow": { "blur": 20 } } }
```

**How a patch merges.** A key you leave out keeps its value, inside a nested object too, so `{shadow: {blur: 20}}` keeps the shadow's colour, angle and distance. On a clip that has no shadow yet, the keys you left out take the defaults listed below. `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection`, `spotlight`, `motion`, `look`, `cursor`, `cutout` and `hide_silent` set to `null` clear that property. `filters` and `obscure` are lists, so each replaces whole: send the full list, or `[]` to clear it. See [Patches](/mcp/patches/).

**Colours.** A colour is four numbers, `[r, g, b, a]`, each 0 to 1. Three numbers are refused, and so is a value outside the range. The chroma key's colour is the one exception: three numbers, with no alpha.

**What it answers.** The usual edit answer: `ok` and the `project` summary. If the patch changes nothing, the call says so and leaves no undo step. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/).

**When it refuses.**

- A key or value the patch doesn't know is an error naming its dotted path, array indices included, and the value you sent, such as `filters[1].kind`. Nothing is dropped, corrected or clamped.
- A number outside its range is an error naming the key, the range and the number.
- A clip with no video properties is an error: "clip 7 has no video properties".
- The sections below list what a particular kind of clip can't take.

### Which key does what

| Keys | Section |
| --- | --- |
| `x`, `y`, `scale`, `rotation`, `opacity`, `blend` | [Transform](#transform-position-scale-rotation-opacity-and-blend) |
| `crop`, `corner_radius` | [Crop and corners](#crop-and-corners) |

### On an adjustment clip

An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) has no picture of its own. Only `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, the sepia, noir, vignette and invert filters, and `opacity` (the grade's strength) do anything there, and `qualifier` narrows which pixels they reach. The blur, sharpen and pixelate filters and any blend mode are errors, such as "clip 7 is an adjustment clip and cannot take the blur filter".

### Animate a property

`set_video` changes the clip's base value, which holds for the clip's whole length. To change a value over time, use `add_action` then `set_action_end`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/). `motion` and `hide_silent` can't be animated.

## Transform: position, scale, rotation, opacity and blend

The clip's picture is centred on the canvas centre plus `x` and `y`, scaled, then rotated about that same centre. The [Transform section](/canvas/transform/) and dragging on the canvas change the same values.

| Key | What it does | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `x`, `y` | The clip's centre, in canvas pixels from the canvas centre. `y` runs down. | Any number |
| `scale` | The size. 1 is native pixels. | 0.01 to 10 |
| `rotation` | Degrees about the clip's centre. Positive turns clockwise on screen. | Any number |
| `opacity` | How solid the clip is. | 0 to 1 |
| `blend` | How the clip combines with what's already on the canvas. | `normal`, `multiply`, `screen`, `add`, `overlay`, `darken`, `lighten`, `difference` |

`normal` is the default. A blend mode needs something under it. Over the empty canvas, `multiply`, `darken` and `overlay` read black, while `screen`, `add`, `lighten` and `difference` change nothing, so `add_background` is usually the call to make first.

A blend is forced to `normal` for the length of a cross dissolve, so the frame there can differ from the value `get_project` reports. A nest clip can't take a blend mode other than `normal`. See [Blend modes](/canvas/blend-modes/).

## Crop and corners

| Key | What it does | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crop` | `{l, t, r, b}`, the pixels to remove from each edge of the source. Cropping never shifts what's left. | Each 0 or more |
| `corner_radius` | Rounds the corners of the cropped picture, in source pixels, before it's rotated. | 0 or more |

The opposite edges have to leave something behind: `l` plus `r` must be less than the source's width, and `t` plus `b` less than its height. See [Crop](/canvas/crop/) and [Corner radius](/canvas/corner-radius/).

## Effects: shadow, chroma key, filters, reflection, spotlight and obscure

Each of these is off until you set it. `shadow`, `chroma`, `reflection` and `spotlight` are objects that merge, and `null` clears one. `filters` and `obscure` are lists that replace whole.

### Shadow

`shadow` is `null` or an object. See [Shadow](/effects/shadow/).

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | The shadow's colour. | Four numbers | Black |
| `opacity` | How strong it is. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |
| `blur` | How soft it is, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 12 |
| `angle` | The direction, in degrees. 0 is to the right, turning counter-clockwise. | Any number | 315 |
| `distance` | How far it falls, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 8 |

### Chroma key

`chroma` is `null` or an object. See [Chroma Key](/effects/chroma-key/).

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | The colour to remove, as three numbers with no alpha. | Each 0 to 1 | Green, `[0, 1, 0]` |
| `tolerance` | How far from the key a colour can be and still go. | 0 to 1 | 0.2 |
| `softness` | How gradually the edge falls off. | 0 to 1 | 0.1 |
| `spill` | How much of the key's colour to take off what's left. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |

### Filters

`filters` is a list of up to four `{kind, amount}` objects, applied in order, so blur then sepia differs from sepia then blur. `kind` is `blur`, `sharpen`, `pixelate`, `sepia`, `noir`, `vignette` or `invert`. `amount` is 0 to 1, where 0 does nothing. A left-out `kind` is `blur` and a left-out `amount` is 0.5. A fifth filter is an error, never dropped. See [Filters](/effects/filters/).

```json
{ "filters": [{ "kind": "noir", "amount": 1 }, { "kind": "vignette", "amount": 0.4 }] }
```

### Reflection

`reflection` is `null` or an object. See [Reflection](/effects/reflection/).

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `opacity` | How strong the reflection is where it touches the clip. | 0 to 1 | 0.35 |
| `height` | How much of the clip is mirrored, as a fraction of its cropped height. | 0 to 1 | 0.5 |
| `gap` | The space between the clip and the reflection, in source pixels. | 0 or more | 0 |
| `falloff` | How fast it fades, as a fraction of the cropped height. 0 doesn't fade, and 1 reaches transparent exactly at `height`. | 0 to 1 | 1 |

### Spotlight

`spotlight` is `null` or an object. It dims everything outside a shape and can magnify what's inside it. See [Spotlight](/effects/spotlight/).

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | The shape. | `rect`, `ellipse` | `rect` |
| `x`, `y` | The shape's centre, in source pixels from the centre of the cropped picture, `y` down. It can sit outside the picture. | Any number | 0 |
| `width`, `height` | The shape's size, in source pixels. | Above 0 | 480, 270 |
| `feather` | How many source pixels the edge blurs over. | 0 or more | 40 |
| `dim` | How much darker it is outside. 0 changes nothing, and 1 is black. | 0 to 1 | 0.6 |
| `zoom` | How much to magnify what's inside. 1 is no zoom. | 1 to 2 | 1 |

Because the box is in source pixels, it stays on the picture when the clip is moved, scaled or rotated.

### Obscure

`obscure` is a list of up to four regions, each hiding what's under it. It uses the spotlight's frame for its centre and box. See [Obscure](/effects/obscure/).

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shape` | The shape. | `rect`, `ellipse` | `rect` |
| `x`, `y` | The region's centre, in source pixels from the centre of the cropped picture. | Any number | 0 |
| `width`, `height` | The region's size, in source pixels. | Above 0 | 480, 270 |
| `feather` | How many source pixels the effect ramps in over. | 0 or more | 20 |
| `kind` | How it hides. | `blur`, `pixelate` | `pixelate` |
| `amount` | How strongly it hides. | 0 to 1 | 1 |

## `cutout`

Remove Background: draws the clip as its subject alone, from masks made on your Mac. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Remove Background** and the Picture sub-tab's **Background** section. See [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/).

`cutout` is `null` or an object. `{cutout: {}}` turns it on with all five defaults, an object merges, and `null` removes it.

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subject` | What to keep. `foreground` is the picture's foreground object, and only an image clip can take it. | `person`, `foreground` | `person` |
| `quality` | The mask quality. `best` is refused, because Best masks aren't made yet. | `standard` | `standard` |
| `background` | `remove` draws only the subject. `keep` draws the clip whole, which [Text Behind Subject](#behind_subject) uses. | `remove`, `keep` | `remove` |
| `edge` | Shrinks or grows the outline. | −1 to 1 | 0 |
| `feather` | Softens the outline. | 0 to 1 | 0 |

A media, still or image clip can take a cutout. A text, shape, graphic, adjustment or nest clip is refused, and so is `foreground` on a media or still clip.

**When the masks are made.** They're made as soon as the cutout is set, and `analyze_cutout` says where they stand. See [Tools: reading analysis](/mcp/tools-analysis/). The cut-out draws in the preview, `render_frame` and every export:

- The preview draws a frame whole while its mask isn't made yet.
- `render_frame` waits up to 30 s for its masks, then draws the clip uncut and says so.
- An export waits for every mask it draws.
- A stretch of the clip where no person was found draws uncut.

**In an action.** `edge` and `feather` animate, and `background` switches when the action ends. `subject` and `quality` are refused there, and an action can't switch the cutout off. On a clip with no cutout, an action's cutout keys do nothing.

## `behind_subject`

Text Behind Subject: `true` cuts the clip at each moment by the person of every cut-out clip on a track behind it in the same container, so the person stands in front of it. A cut-out clip in front of it doesn't cut it. Any clip with a cutout counts, with `background` set to `remove` or `keep`. The default is `false`. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Behind Subject** section. See [Text Behind Subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).

Any clip that draws a picture can take it, except an adjustment clip or a nest clip, which are refused. In an action it switches when the action ends. [`text_behind_subject`](/mcp/tools-clip-properties/) places a title this way in one step.

## `cursor`

Styles the cursor recorded in the media's cursor file, as it's drawn on this clip. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Cursor** section. See [Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/).

`cursor` is `null` or an object. `{cursor: {}}` stores all eight defaults, and an object merges. A value out of range is refused, never clamped.

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `show` | Whether the cursor is drawn. | `true`, `false` | `true` |
| `scale` | Its size. | 0.25 to 8 | 1 |
| `style` | `recorded` draws the recorded image, and `arrow` draws Frame Job's own arrow. `recorded` also draws the arrow at a moment the file holds no cursor image. | `recorded`, `arrow` | `recorded` |
| `smoothing` | How much the path is smoothed. | 0 to 1 | 0 |
| `hide_idle` | Seconds of no activity before it hides. `null` never hides it. | `null`, 0.5 to 30 | `null` |
| `clicks` | What a click draws. | `none`, `ripple` | `none` |
| `click_color` | The ripple's colour, as a CSS colour. | Any CSS colour | `#ffffffcc` |
| `click_size` | The ripple's size. | 0.25 to 4 | 1 |

**In an action.** `scale` and `click_size` animate. `show`, `style`, `clicks` and `click_color` switch when the action ends. `smoothing` and `hide_idle` have no effect in an action, so write them here. On a clip with no cursor, every cursor key in an action switches at the end, so give the clip one first with `{cursor: {}}` if you want them to animate.

## `motion`

What the clip does on its way in, on its way out and all the way through. It mirrors **Clip ▸ Motion ▸**. See [Motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/).

`motion` is `null` or `{in, out, during}`. The three slots merge: a slot you leave out keeps what's stored, a slot set to `null` clears that slot, and `{motion: null}` clears all three.

| Slot | Keys | Values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in`, `out` | `kind`, `duration` | `kind` is `fade`, `zoom_in`, `zoom_out`, `slide_left`, `slide_right`, `slide_up`, `slide_down`, `spin` or `pop`. `duration` is in ticks, measured from the clip's first or last frame. |
| `during` | `kind`, `amount`, `period` | `kind` is `pulse`, `shake`, `spin`, `bounce` or `drift`. `amount` is 0 to 1. `period` is in ticks, and `drift` ignores it. |

```json
{ "motion": { "in": { "kind": "fade", "duration": 300000 }, "during": null } }
```

A slot you name without its keys starts from a half-second `fade`, or for `during` a `pulse` of amount 0.5 and period 1 s.

The durations snap to the frame grid, and the period snaps with a floor of one frame, so `get_project` can answer with a number near the one you sent. `in` plus `out` longer than the clip scales both down to meet, rather than being refused. A negative duration, or a period under one tick, is an error.

`motion` can't be animated: `set_action_end` refuses it. `get_project` reports the clip as if it weren't moving, because the preset only becomes placement when a frame is drawn.

## `motion_blur`

Blurs the clip, and its moving cursor, along their motion. It mirrors the **Motion Blur** row in the Picture sub-tab's **Transform** section. See [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/).

`motion_blur` is 0 to 1, the shutter as a fraction of one canvas frame. 0 is off and the default, and 0.5 is a 180° shutter. It animates in an action, and draws in the preview, `render_frame` and every export.

Anything above 0 is refused on a nest clip, so set it on the clips inside, and on an adjustment clip. The clip draws sharp under a transition, a routed dissolve, a matte, Behind Subject or a drop shadow.

## `hide_silent`

Fades the clip out while a media's speech is silent, and back in just before it speaks. It's usually a camera over a screen recording. It mirrors the Picture sub-tab's **Hide While Silent** section. See [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/).

`hide_silent` is `null` or an object.

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `media` | Required. The id of the media, with sound, whose speech the clip follows. | A media id | |
| `pre_roll` | How long before speech the clip is fully in, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 120,000 (0.2 s) |
| `hold` | How long after speech it stays, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 900,000 (1.5 s) |
| `fade` | How long the fade takes, in ticks. | 0 to 3,000,000 (5 s) | 180,000 (0.3 s) |

```json
{ "hide_silent": { "media": 3, "hold": 600000 } }
```

The fade follows the clips of that media in the nearest container where one plays: the clip's own, then each nest around it. Where none plays, the clip stays visible. These three times don't snap to the frame grid.

If the media has no saved speech, this call saves it from the on-device voice detection first, in the same undo step. It's refused when the media has no sound, when its speech hasn't been detected yet ("Try again in a moment."), and on a nest clip, so set it on the clips inside.

Only the drawn frame sees the fade: `get_project` reads the clip's opacity without it. `hide_silent` can't be animated.

## `color`

The thirteen values of the Color sub-tab's **Light** and **Color** sections, in one object. Each is 0 for unchanged, and any subset merges. See [Light](/color/light/) and [Brightness, contrast, saturation and hue](/color/color-section/).

| Key | What it does | Range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exposure` | Exposure, in stops. | −3 to 3 |
| `temperature` | Positive is warmer. | −1 to 1 |
| `tint` | Positive is more magenta. | −1 to 1 |
| `highlights` | The upper half of the brightness range. | −1 to 1 |
| `shadows` | The lower half of the brightness range. | −1 to 1 |
| `whites` | Stretches the picture, held at black. | −1 to 1 |
| `blacks` | Stretches the picture, held at white. | −1 to 1 |
| `vibrance` | Saturation on the colours that have little. | −1 to 1 |
| `fade` | Lifts black towards 10 % and lowers white towards 95 %. | 0 to 1 |
| `brightness` | Brightness. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
| `contrast` | Contrast. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
| `saturation` | Saturation. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −1 to 1. |
| `hue` | Turns every colour's hue this many degrees, red towards yellow towards green, keeping its Rec. 709 brightness. | Any number. The inspector's row runs −180 to 180. |

A value outside a stated range is refused.

The grade runs in this order: `color`, `wheels`, `curves`, `look`, then `filters`.

## `wheels`

Lift, gamma and gain: three colour pushes, each with its own brightness. An agent can set a push as exact numbers, which the [Wheels section](/color/wheels/) has no field for.

`wheels` is `{lift, gamma, gain}`, each `{x, y, master}`, each −1 to 1, with 0 unchanged. Any subset merges, so `{wheels: {lift: {x: 0.2, y: -0.1}}}` keeps lift's `master` and the other two wheels.

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `x`, `y` | The colour push. Its angle is the hue (0° red, 120° green, 240° blue), and its length is the strength. It must lie inside the unit circle, so `x²` plus `y²` is at most 1. |
| `master` | The brightness. |

`lift` moves black and holds white, `gain` moves white and holds black, and `gamma` moves the middle and holds both ends. A value outside these limits is refused, never clamped.

## `curves`

Writes the curves of the Color sub-tab's **Curves** section, one list of points per channel. See [Master and RGB curves](/color/curves/) and [Hue vs Hue and Hue vs Sat curves](/color/hue-curves/).

`curves` is an object with up to six channels. A list replaces that channel whole, and `null` removes it. Each list is 2 to 16 `[x, y]` points with `x` strictly rising.

| Channel | `x` | `y` | No change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `master`, `red`, `green`, `blue` | 0 to 1 | 0 to 1 | `y` equals `x` from 0 to 1 |
| `hue_hue` | Hue in degrees, 0 up to but not including 360 | A shift in degrees, −180 to 180 | Every `y` is 0 |
| `hue_sat` | Hue in degrees, 0 up to but not including 360 | A saturation gain, 0 to 2 | Every `y` is 1 |

```json
{ "curves": { "master": [[0, 0.05], [0.5, 0.55], [1, 1]], "hue_sat": null } }
```

A curve that changes nothing is stored as no curve. A point outside these limits is refused, never clamped.

The tone channels are smooth monotone curves through their points, flat outside the first and last `x`, and a colour goes through the colour channel after `master`. The two hue curves are smooth curves that wrap at 0 and 360. They run after the tone channels, on the colour's hue read once: a positive shift turns red towards yellow towards green, keeping brightness, and the gain scales saturation. Greys are left alone, and the effect fades in up to a chroma of 0.06.

In an action, a curve that changes nothing animates to neutral, and two curves with different point counts blend their values across the action.

## `look`

Applies one of the eight built-in looks, or an imported `.cube` LUT, at an amount. It mirrors the Color sub-tab's **Look** section and **Clip ▸ Look ▸**. See [Looks](/color/looks/) and [.cube LUTs](/color/luts/).

`look` is `null` or an object. `{look: null}` removes it.

| Key | What it does | Range | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | Which look. | `warm`, `cool`, `teal_orange`, `vivid`, `faded`, `vintage`, `dramatic`, `black_white`, `lut` | |
| `media` | The media id of the `.cube` file. Required with `lut`, and refused with any other kind. | A LUT's media id | |
| `amount` | How much of it. | 0 to 1 | 1 |

```json
{ "look": { "kind": "teal_orange", "amount": 0.6 } }
```

For a LUT, bring the file in with `import_media`, then send `{look: {kind: "lut", media: 9}}` with the id it answers.

A new kind keeps the clip's amount, and a built-in kind replaces a LUT. An amount alone needs a clip that already has a look. In an action the amount animates, and a change of kind or of LUT switches when the action ends.

## `qualifier`

Narrows which pixels an adjustment clip's grade reaches, by hue, saturation and luma. It mirrors the Color sub-tab's **Qualifier** section. See [Qualifiers](/color/qualifiers/).

The qualifier is for adjustment clips only. On any other clip it's an error naming the clip. It reads the picture behind the clip, before the grade.

`qualifier` is `{hue, saturation, luma, invert, blur}`.

| Key | Keys inside it | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hue` | `center`, `width`, `softness` | In degrees. `center` is 0 to 360 and wraps. `width` is 0 to 360, fully selected about the centre. `softness` is 0 to 180, the fall-off outside each edge. A colour with a chroma under about 0.06 has no hue and is never selected by it. |
| `saturation` | `low`, `high`, `softness` | Each 0 to 1, with `low` no more than `high`. Near-black reads as 0. |
| `luma` | `low`, `high`, `softness` | Each 0 to 1, with `low` no more than `high`. Rec. 709 luma. |
| `invert` | | `true` selects everything else. |
| `blur` | | 0 to 1, 0 being off. Softens the selection by a Gaussian of 24 × `blur` canvas pixels, never the matte. It draws nothing with no range on. |

A range merges: `{hue: {}}` turns hue on at centre 30, width 50, softness 25, and saturation and luma turn on at low 0, high 1, softness 0.1. A partial range keeps the rest, and `null` turns a range off. The selection is the product of the ranges that are on. A value outside its bounds is refused, never clamped.

In an action the numbers animate, the hue centre taking the short way round, so 350 to 10 passes 0. A range turned on or off, and `invert`, switch when the action ends.

`render_frame` with `selection` set to the adjustment clip's id draws what the qualifier selects, as [Show Selection](/color/show-selection/) does. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
